result.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces
result.summary: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next. We present Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS) for set pieces, which treats a corner or a lofted free kick as a distribution over plausible executions and plausible futures instead of a single realised event. From the pre-kick state, MCPS proposes counterfactual deliveries and counterfactual set-ups (where the attackers stand at the kick), plays each out many times in a world model (3D ball physics, a generative model of all 22 players, the keeper's come-or-stay decision and a Player-to-Touch model) and scores every future with a value model. On 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches, with every model applied only to matches it never saw, the best available delivery is worth 0.0085 xG more than the one kicked (+28 %), mainly because it reaches an attacker before the keeper. Searching where the attackers stand as well adds +0.0027 xG with the observed ball and +0.0033 on top of the best ball; designing their runs too adds +0.0007 more. We show how to keep such a search honest, and estimate how much more data each component needs before a club could rely on it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Monte Carlo Pass Search，将角球和长传任意球视为执行与未来结局的分布：从踢球前状态生成反事实传球与进攻站位，在世界模型中多次推演，并用价值模型为每个未来打分，在 30 场 Serie A 比赛上比较最优方案与真实执行的 xG 差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「候选提议—多次 rollout—价值模型打分」的反事实搜索与防止搜索偏差的评估思路，可能为 LVR 中候选 latent 假设的生成、展开验证与选择提供类比线索，但论文不涉及视觉推理，迁移价值需较多核查。
